newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seizes cocaine in Disney book shipment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seizes cocaine in Disney book shipment.

text.p: U.S. agents seized $12 million worth of cocaine smuggled from Colombia in a ship container filled with cartons of the Disney book "101 Dalmations," officials said on Wednesday.

U.S. Customs Service Special Agent Marty Ficke said investigators determined the Walt Disney Co and the importer and exporter of the books were not involved in smuggling the 806 pounds (366 kgs) of cocaine.

Customs Service and Drug Enforcement Administration agents made the seizure on Jan. 21 but it was not made public until Wednesday because of an ongoing investigation, Ficke said. He said arrests would be made soon.

The seizure was made at a warehouse in Edison, New Jersey, where agents found the cocaine concealed in eight duffle bags on the floor of the container, hidden under the book cartons, Ficke said. The cocaine had a street value of $12 million.
The container carrying 876 cartons of books arrived in the United States at Howland Hook, New Jersey, from Colombia and was destined for a book company in Mansfield, Massachusetts, the agent said.
